challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to .faff/ at all, not only committing them. Caching resolved API keys in .faff/cache/credentials.json writes literal secrets to disk under .faff/, which the old decision explicitly prohibits. Being gitignored does not answer the guarantee: the file can still be read by other local processes, swept into backups, artifacts or logs, and outlives the environment. The why never engages with the old rationale and offers only an unmeasured small latency gain against reading process.env, which is an in-memory lookup. The supersession argument is unsound.
